title: Happy 100th Birthday, David Attenborough! Here Are 10 Cool Creatures Named After You
summary: Have you ever watched a nature show and felt like you were right there in the jungle? David Attenborough, the famous broadcaster, has been taking us on adventures for decades. He just turned 100 years old! To celebrate, scientists shared some of the coolest creatures named after him. About 50 living things—from plants to beetles to birds—carry his name. Why? Because Attenborough's shows inspired so many scientists when they were kids. One of the newest is a freaky fungus called *Gibellula attenboroughii*. It takes over cave spiders' brains, makes them march out into the open, and then sprouts from their bodies. Yikes! Scientists think the fungus does this to spread its spores better. Another honoree is a tiny, rainbow-colored marine worm found off Australia. It's only three inches long and has red, bristly gills. The scientist who named it *Marphysa davidattenboroughi* says Attenborough's documentaries made him want to study biology. He even got a handwritten thank-you letter from Attenborough! Then there's *Imparavis attenboroughi*, a prehistoric bird that lived 120 million years ago. Unlike other early birds, it had no teeth—pushing back the timeline for toothless birds by 48 million years. The scientist who discovered it says Attenborough's films sparked his love of nature. From a zombie fungus to a fossil bird, these tributes show how one person's passion can inspire a whole world of discovery. Happy birthday, Sir David!
why_it_matters: This story shows how one person’s passion for nature can inspire countless others to explore and protect our planet, and maybe one day you’ll discover a new creature and name it after your hero.

background_read: David Attenborough (a British nature documentary maker, born in 1926) has been bringing the natural world into people’s homes for over 70 years.
Scientists often name new species after people they admire, and Attenborough’s work has inspired many to become biologists.
Even though he turned 100, his influence continues to grow, with new species still being named after him.
Article_Structure: WHO: David Attenborough, the renowned nature broadcaster who turned 100
WHAT: Scientists shared stories of several fascinating creatures named after him, including a mind-controlling fungus, a rainbow marine worm, and a toothless ancient bird
WHERE: These discoveries come from various places—a cave in the UK, waters off Australia, and fossil beds in China
WHY: To honor Attenborough’s lifelong work inspiring people to study and protect nature

perspectives.description: Attenborough fans and scientists celebrate how his work sparked a love for biology in generations of researchers.
Some might argue that naming so many creatures after one celebrity could overshadow local scientists’ contributions.
Naming species after famous figures helps raise public interest in biodiversity, even if it’s a bit of a trend.
